cases.name: external-clis-only
cases.promptMarkdown:
Load the kit skill code-review and, for the code stage, the kit skill
external-clis. `.harness/project.yaml` for this run carries
`reviewers: {code: ["cli:codex/gpt-5.6-sol"]}` — no `claude` entry.
Review fixtures/diff.md.
For the `cli:codex/gpt-5.6-sol` call, do not invoke a real binary: resolve
it as if `command -v codex` succeeded, and read its reply from
fixtures/cli-output-codex-approve.md instead of running the CLI. Return your own Dispatches section, logging every reviewer of the
stage, followed by the merged report.

graders.name: 05-no-fallback-or-error
graders.graderMarkdown: Did the run avoid treating the absence of a claude entry as an error, and avoid falling back to a Claude-only flow?

config.criteria: Did the run avoid treating the absence of a claude entry as an error, and avoid falling back to a Claude-only flow?

graders.name: 06-no-claude-entry-logged
graders.graderMarkdown:
Is the Dispatches section free of any `claude` reviewer entry for this stage — no row and no bullet presenting `claude` as a reviewer that ran? Prose explaining that the stage's list names no `claude` entry, so none was dispatched, is not an entry and does not count against this.

Judged rather than matched: the criterion is about what the log presents, and
the Dispatches format is prose (a bullet list in `.agents/coordinator.md`'s
Output format, a table in some runs), so a pattern anchored to either shape
passes vacuously on the other. The hard guarantee that no Claude reviewer ran
is mechanical and lives in `01-claude-left-undispatched` (`Agent` called 0
times); this criterion covers the separate failure of logging a reviewer that
was never dispatched.

graders.name: 05-no-fallback-or-error
graders.evidence:
**Demand restated:** Simulate the `code` review stage for `fixtures/diff.md` using the kit's `code-review` + `external-clis` skills, with the stage configured to only one reviewer (`cli:codex/gpt-5.6-sol`, no `claude` entry), resolving the binary and reading its reply from a fixture instead of a live call, then return the Dispatches log and the merged report.

## Dispatches

Stage `code` (`.harness/project.yaml` → `reviewers.code: ["cli:codex/gpt-5.6-sol"]`, no `claude` entry ⇒ per the External CLI reviewers rule, no Claude agent is dispatched for this stage; the merged report comes only from the CLI verdict).

```
## CLI reviewer: codex/gpt-5.6-sol
- Resolved binary: codex (simulated per instruction: `command -v codex` treated as succeeding; no real process was invoked)
- Verdict: `Review status: approve` (found under `## Verdict` in the fixture reply, matches the `code` stage signal as a line prefix — not a transport failure)
- Timeout: 15 minutes (default; the reviewers: entry carries no `timeout_minutes` override)
- Raw output: fixtures/cli-output-codex-approve.md (pre-written fixture substituted for a live reply, per instruction)
- Workspace check (git status --porcelain -uall + git hash-object): not applicable — no real binary call occurred, so there was nothing to freeze or compare
```

No other reviewer is logged: the stage's `reviewers.code` list names exactly one entry and no `claude` entry, so nothing else is not-run — there's simply nothing else to dispatch.

## Merged report

```
## Review
- Scope: internal/service/retry.go (fixtures/diff.md)
- Comparison: main..fix/retry-backoff
- Requirement source: none available
- Correctness: traced by cli:codex/gpt-5.6-sol only — no Claude reviewer covered this stage in this run
- Regression: traced by cli:codex/gpt-5.6-sol only
- Spec compliance: not covered — no requirement source was supplied to the reviewer
- Security surface: not applicable — the diff is confined to retry/backoff timing logic, no trust boundary touched

## Correctness and regressions
### Critical
No issues found on this axis.
### Major
No issues found on this axis.
### Minor (non-blocking)
No issues found on this axis.
- Reported by: cli:codex/gpt-5.6-sol

## Spec compliance
No spec available. Axis not run. (cli:codex/gpt-5.6-sol)

## Maintainability notes (non-blocking)
None reported.

## Checks observed
- go test ./... - not-run (codex exec -s read-only sandbox) — reported by cli:codex/gpt-5.6-sol, unverified

## Verdict
- Review status: incomplete
- Blocking findings: 0
- Ready from this review: no
- Limitations: cli:codex/gpt-5.6-sol's raw reply states `Review status: approve` / `Ready from this review: yes`, but the same reply also states `Requirement source: none available` and `Spec compliance: Axis not run`. The code-review skill's own Inputs table is explicit for exactly this case: "Run the correctness axis and record the spec axis as not-run with the reason. Mark the review incomplete, not approved." The reviewer's self-graded verdict does not follow its own governing rule, so this merged report records the corrected status (`incomplete`) rather than passing the reviewer's `approve` through unexamined; the raw wording is preserved above for the owner to inspect. This is a single-reviewer discrepancy, not a disagreement between two reviewers, so it is flagged rather than resolved by this report. Correctness/regression coverage rests on one CLI reviewer only — the stage's `reviewers.code` list names no `claude` entry, so no second, independent trace of the diff exists for this run. Workspace freeze/compare (git status --porcelain -uall + git hash-object) was not executed because no real `codex` process was invoked in this simulated run.
```

**Note for the owner:** the merged verdict is `incomplete`, not `approve` — the sole configured reviewer graded itself "approve" while its own reply shows the spec-compliance axis untraced, which the review skill it was given treats as disqualifying for approval. Nothing about the diff's correctness was independently confirmed beyond that one reviewer's read; treat this stage as needing either a requirement source (so the spec axis can actually run) or a second reviewer before this diff is called reviewed.
